title: Peptide serum and bakuchiol serum: what they are and how to use them
body:
Peptides and bakuchiol are two of the most searched serum ingredients in the UK, often alongside ceramides. They do different jobs and suit different routines. Here is what each one is, how to use a peptide serum or a bakuchiol serum, and the serums we stock that contain them.

What are peptides?

Peptides are short chains of amino acids, the building blocks of proteins. In skincare they are made in the lab or taken from plants, and they usually appear in serums and creams in small amounts. Different peptides have different trade names, such as Matrixyl or Argireline, so a peptide serum often lists several of them together.

Peptide serums we stock

  • Highborn London YOUTHBOOST Peptide Serum (£94) combines four peptide ingredients in one lightweight, vegan-friendly serum: Matrixyl 3000, Argireline, Tripeptide-5 and Copper Tripeptide-1 (a copper peptide).
  • Caviar Serum with 24K Gold (£34.99) is a Swansura Selection serum with tremella polysaccharide, beta-glucan and sodium hyaluronate for hydration, aloe vera and oat kernel extract, amino acids and peptides, carnosine and 24K gold leaf.

What is bakuchiol?

Bakuchiol is a plant-derived ingredient, taken from the seeds of the babchi plant (Psoralea corylifolia). It is often chosen instead of retinol by people who prefer a plant-based ingredient. It can usually be used morning and night; as with any new serum, patch test first.

Bakuchiol serums we stock

  • Highborn London Bakuchiol Youth Elixir (£99) is a bakuchiol serum made in England for mature and sensitive skin, for morning or evening use.
  • Vilvah Better Ageing Serum (£28.99, 20ml) has the longest list: bakuchiol and a natural peptide extract (from sacha inchi seed), with blue pea flower extract, pomegranate seed oil, hyaluronic acid, two ceramides, niacinamide and olive squalane. It brings peptides, bakuchiol and ceramides together in one bottle, in a light texture.

What are ceramides?

Ceramides are lipids that occur naturally in the outer layer of skin. In skincare they are added to help skin feel smooth and comfortable, and they pair well with peptides or bakuchiol. Highborn London MOISTUREBURST Hydrating Glow Ceramide Serum (from £57, 30ml or 50ml) is a lightweight ceramide serum for dry, dehydrated and mature skin, made to layer under moisturiser.

How to use a peptide or bakuchiol serum

  1. Cleanse and, if you use one, apply toner. Our face wash guide and toner guide help you choose.
  2. Apply 2 or 3 drops of serum to the face and neck and press it in.
  3. Follow with moisturiser, such as Highborn London Imperial Moisturiser (£46). See moisturiser for your skin type.
  4. In the morning, finish with SPF, for example Vilvah Skin Finish Sunscreen SPF 50 PA+++ (£17.99).

Use one new serum at a time, so you know what suits your skin. One serum in the morning and one at night is plenty for most people.

Can you use peptides and bakuchiol together?

Yes, they are commonly layered, and the Vilvah Better Ageing Serum already contains both. If you use two serums, apply the thinner, watery one first and the richer one after, or use one in the morning and one at night.

Ready-made routines

  • The Vilvah Better Ageing Kit (£48.99) pairs the Better Ageing Serum with the Ultra Moisturising Cream (glycerine, olive squalane, bamboo and goji berry extracts) for an evening routine.
  • The Vilvah Night Repair Kit (£42.99) pairs the same serum with an Under Eye Cream made with shea butter, sunflower seed oil, bamboo and goji berry extracts.

Good to know

  • Patch test any new serum on your jaw or inner arm for 24 hours.
  • Pregnant or breastfeeding? Check new skincare ingredients with your GP or pharmacist first.
  • Stinging, redness or itching that lasts is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.
  • For vitamin C, hyaluronic acid and niacinamide, see our face serum guide.

Shop every serum, or browse Highborn London and Vilvah. Every order ships from the UK, with free UK delivery over £40.
